lesson_title: The Running Total Tells a Different Story
hook_text: A stokvel treasurer keeps two columns: this month's money, and the total so far. One of them is secretly a matric graph.
clip_script: Every stokvel treasurer keeps two columns. Column one: what came in THIS month. Column two: the total SO FAR. Same money — completely different stories. March's deposit tells you how good March was. The running total tells you when the fund crossed ten thousand rand. Now here's the thing: statistics does exactly this with data. The histogram is column one — how many learners in EACH band of travel times. The ogive is column two — how many SO FAR — drawn as a curve. Six learners under ten minutes. Sixteen under twenty. Thirty under thirty. Thirty-seven, then all forty. Plot each total at the END of its class — because the total is only complete when the whole class is counted — and you get a lazy S that climbs and never, ever comes downhill. A running total cannot shrink. If your ogive dips, you subtracted in a column that only adds. And that curve is a machine: slide across from position twenty, drop down — there's your median, about twenty-three minutes, read straight off the graph. No formula. Just the treasurer's second column doing matric statistics.
visual_style: A stokvel ledger book animates: monthly deposits stack as histogram bars while a glowing running-total line climbs into a lazy-S ogive; a dotted ruler line slides across from 20 and drops to the median.
pacing: Steady ledger setup, quickening as the totals stack, a beat on 'never comes downhill', smooth glide for the ruler move.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and read medians, quartiles and percentiles straight off the curve.
